title: Naturality of the shared scheme derived tensor symmetry
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. The shared K-flat derived tensor on D(O_X) [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure] admits isomorphisms s(K,L): K tensor^L L to L tensor^L K such that for all derived morphisms a:K to K′ and b:L to L′, (a tensor b);s(K′,L′) = s(K,L);(b tensor a).

proof.text: Install exactly the underived tensor, symmetric structure, additive and closed propositions of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed], Grothendieck structure, small colimits and functorial flat-resolution theorem used in [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. The upstream DerivedCategory.hasDerivedMonoidalCategory then supplies the shared localization tensor. Use DerivedMonoidal.braiding for Qh and quasi-isomorphisms; this constructs the isomorphisms rather than choosing arbitrary existence witnesses.

Expand tensorHom_def, apply DerivedMonoidal.braiding_naturality_right and braiding_naturality_left, reassociate, and use tensorHom_def' to recover the reversed tensor map. This proves simultaneous naturality.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_schemeDerivedTensorSymmetry (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))] :
    ∃ s : ∀ K L : schemeDerivedCategory X, K ⊗ L ≅ L ⊗ K,
      ∀ (K K' L L' : schemeDerivedCategory X) (a : K ⟶ K') (b : L ⟶ L'),
        (a ⊗ₘ b) ≫ (s K' L').hom = (s K L).hom ≫ (b ⊗ₘ a)
